A few items we need to get moving on from our side so engineering can schedule the work: 
- Private connectivity: we want a VPC endpoint or private peering so requests to the Redwood API don't egress over the public internet.
- IP allowlist: our security team needs the full set of IP ranges or a hostname we can pin.

- Embeddings + reranker: expected endpoints and throughput assumptions (we'll be batching).

Attached is a short PDF with our initial compliance checklist (catalyx_requirements.pdf). Can you share a proposed implementation checklist and an estimated timeline for air-gapped-friendly private connect + SDK onboarding?

Aisha — thanks for the clear list and the PDF, that helps a lot. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

Recap (high level):
- Redwood can provide PrivateLink-style endpoints (AWS), Private Service Connect (GCP), or on-premises connector for air-gapped customers.
- We support IP allowlisting and/or private DNS records pointing to the private endpoint; we can provide CIDR ranges or a stable internal hostname depending on the provider.
- mTLS is supported for customer-to-Redwood traffic; we'll exchange certs via secure SFTP/Drive link and provide a short rotation playbook.
- SDK auth: recommend service-account-like tokens for server-to-server integrations (short-lived tokens + refresh flow) — we'll include an example implementation.
- Embeddings & rerank: embeddings will be a separate endpoint with batching guidance; reranker flow typically sits behind a small scoring service and calls Redwood for both embeddings and generate/rerank.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Kickoff tech session (30–45m) with Priyom (solutions) + your network engineer to capture network details and cert exchange plan. 
2) We’ll circulate a Mutual Action Plan (attached) with milestone dates — please add your procurement owner.
3) Priyom will share a network diagram and a template IP allowlist + mTLS cert exchange instructions.
4) We’ll scope expected throughput and give a recommended autoscaling/batching config for your initial POC.

Suggested times for a kickoff next week (PT): Tue 6/20 10:00 or Wed 6/21 14:00 — tell me which works and I’ll lock it in.

Subject: Technical follow-up: network + SDK notes for Catalyx

Hi Aisha/Kim — following up with concrete technical notes that should help your network and infra teams plan. Summary first, details below.

Summary:
- Private endpoint options: AWS PrivateLink (recommended if Catalyx is on AWS), GCP Private Service Connect, or a bridged on-prem connector. PrivateLink gives you a private NLB in our account and an Interface VPC Endpoint in yours.
- DNS & IPs: we can provide a stable internal DNS name (e.g., api.internal.redwood.prod) that resolves to the interface endpoint; if you need IPs we’ll provide the NLB ranges. Expect small changes during cutover; plan for a brief maintenance window.
- mTLS: we require client cert validation for private-connect customers. Steps: you generate a CSR -> we sign (if you want) or exchange public certs -> TLS handshake enforces CN and SAN checks. Rotation: recommend 90-day rotation; we support automated rotation via our control plane if you provide a rotation webhook.
- Auth & SDK: server-to-server flows should use short-lived JWTs minted by your auth service; alternatively a long-lived API key scoped to the project + IP binding is possible for POC only. SDK: our Node/Python SDK supports both approaches; we’ll share code snippets and a small test harness.
- Embeddings and rerank: embeddings endpoint supports batch sizes up to 512 tokens per request; for rerank we recommend 8–16 candidate scoring per call and local caching of vectors to reduce calls. Use our structured output mode when calling external tools to avoid parsing drift.
- Throughput: expect ~120–180 QPS for a single 8-GPU Dedicated pool; we’ll help size initial capacity based on your expected concurrency.

Actionable artifacts I’m attaching: networking-diagram.png (illustrates PrivateLink path + DNS flow) and below are the templates you can hand to your networking team: 

IP Allowlist template (example):
- 10.12.34.0/24 (interface endpoint NLB)
- 10.12.35.0/24 (failover)

mTLS cert exchange (short):
1) Create CSR (use CN=network.catalyx.internal).
2) Send CSR to redwood-secure@redwood-inference.com via SFTP/Drive link.
3) We return signed cert and intermediate in PKCS#12 and PEM.
4) Configure your client to present certs on TLS handshake; we validate CN and SAN.

SDK snippet (Python):
import redwood
client = redwood.Client(endpoint='https://api.internal.redwood.prod', cert=('client.pem', 'client.key'))
resp = client.generate(prompt='Summarize order 123')

I’ll be on the kickoff to walk through the diagram and cert steps.

Priyom
